body: Hello @norsehorse-dev, apparently browsers send extra information when sharing on-screen text (open the key file in a browser -> tap on the text -> select all -> share). Although it's recognized as a key by PGPony, the app shows an error if the extra data is not manually removed. Would be interesting to get rid of the extra data or just read the key string, avoiding an unnecessary error. This could be useful when user unintentionally copies some extra characters. There is no such browser generated extra data when simply using copy-paste. Thanks _Edit: no problem found when sharing a downloaded. asc file via the browser's context menu._

comments.body:
Confirmed, and stripping it is the right fix. The share-from-browser path hands us the selected text plus the page's extra markup, and right now import expects the input to be just the key, so the extra characters trip it. Copy-paste and shared .asc files skip that because they arrive clean.

The fix is to pull the armored block out of whatever is shared, between the BEGIN and END PGP lines, and ignore everything around it, so a select-all-and-share imports the same as a clean paste. Handling more than one block in the payload comes with it.

It is in for the next release. Thanks for pinning down exactly which path adds the noise.

NorseHorse

This shipped in 4.5.0-RC2. Sharing a key to PGPony now pulls the armored block out of whatever the share hands over, between the BEGIN and END lines, and ignores the surrounding page text, so a select-all-and-share imports the same as a clean paste. More than one block in the payload is handled, and it prefers the key block over anything else such as a detached signature.

Installs in place, no uninstall:
https://pgpony.app/rc/4.5.0-RC-foss/PGPony-4.5.0-RC2-foss.apk

If you find a share source that still trips it, tell me where you shared from and I will take a look.

NorseHorse
